title: Statins for people at low risk
authors: Parish E, Bloom T, Godlee F
authorConflicts: All authors are editors of The BMJ.
result: Editorial. In August 2014 an expert panel convened by The BMJ called for anonymised individual patient data from the statin trials to be made available for independent scrutiny. In reply, the Cholesterol Treatment Trialists' Collaboration confirmed that its meta-analyses had been limited to patient-level data on cause-specific mortality, major vascular events and site-specific cancers, that other adverse events were not part of the original agreement, and that trialists agreed in 2013 to pool all adverse events. Of principal investigators of 32 major statin trials contacted by the journal, seven responded. The editors state that guideline producers had not had access to analyses by third parties independent of the trialists, that adverse event data remained the preserve of individual trialists and drug company sponsors, and that the trials were not designed specifically to measure harms. The journal acknowledged that it had published two articles that misrepresented rates of adverse events from statins.
